solutions.check: grid and clues read from the FT's printable PDF, its numbering matching the clue list; every fifteensquared answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Bolt likely to get rusty maybe outside church (needs turning)

indicators.note: outside tells us the damp word goes around the church letters

parts.note: damp conditions make iron likely to rust

indicators.note: the parenthetical says the church abbreviation must be turned round before it goes in

parts.note: CE stands for Church of England

explanation.surface: A bolt that may rust is fitted outside a church, with a note that it needs turning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bolt' looks like a metal fastener but is the verb meaning run away; the bracketed 'needs turning' applies only to the church abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: To bolt is to flee suddenly, and to decamp is to leave in a hurry or secretly.

clue.text: Somehow provides challenge successfully?

indicators.note: somehow suggests the letters are arranged in some other way

explanation.surface: Somebody somehow manages to mount a successful challenge.
explanation.definitionFit: To refute a claim is to show it false, a successful challenge to it.

clue.text: Cold animal crossing a river? It makes a shrill note

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

indicators.note: crossing has the big cat's letters spanning the other pieces

parts.note: a lion is an animal

explanation.surface: A big cat in the cold crosses a river, making a shrill call.
explanation.definitionFit: A clarion is a medieval trumpet with a clear, piercing tone.

clue.text: Duck stuck in mud that's rippled and shiny

indicators.note: stuck in puts the zero letter inside the mud word

parts.note: mire is deep mud
a duck in cricket is a score of nothing, O

explanation.surface: A duck stuck in the mud has wet, glossy feathers.
explanation.walkthrough: A cricket duck is a score of zero, hence O.
explanation.definitionFit: Moire is a watered fabric finish, wavy and lustrous.

clue.text: Mad fellow, one brought to account, Jolson?

parts.note: a fellow is a man
one is the Roman numeral I
Al Jolson was the American singer and entertainer

explanation.surface: A question about whether Al Jolson, a mad fellow, was ever held to account.
explanation.definitionFit: Maniacal describes wild, deranged behaviour, a synonym for crazed.

clue.text: Group of arrows may be very shaky

explanation.surface: An archer's arrows tremble in their case.
explanation.definitionFit: A quiver holds arrows, so its full contents; and the phrase is also an idiom for trembling with excitement.

clue.text: Fire up one politician when standing on Jerusalem's hill

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I
MP is a Member of Parliament
as can mean when, as in 'as he arrived'
Sion (Zion) is the hill of Jerusalem

explanation.surface: A politician fires up a crowd standing on the hill in Jerusalem.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer 'standing on' just places the first pieces above SION.
explanation.definitionFit: To impassion is to stir up strong feelings, to inflame.

clue.text: Drink precedes disturbance in vehicle

indicators.note: precedes means the tea word comes before the disturbance

parts.note: cha is tea
a riot is a disturbance

explanation.surface: A drink is followed by a fracas in a car.
explanation.definitionFit: A chariot is a horse-drawn vehicle of ancient warfare.

clue.text: Theologian left biblical city clutching article

indicators.note: clutching has the city's letters hold the article

parts.note: Ur of the Chaldees, Abraham's city in the Bible
the is the definite article

explanation.surface: A theologian leaves an ancient city, holding an essay.
explanation.definitionFit: Martin Luther was the German divine who started the Reformation.

clue.text: Opera put back on to street arenas

indicators.note: put back tells us the opera's name is written backwards

parts.note: Aida is Verdi's opera

explanation.surface: An opera revival is staged again on the street, in big arenas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put back' gives ADIA; 'on to' here just joins the street abbreviation in front.
explanation.definitionFit: Stadia is a Latin-style plural of stadium, sports arenas.

clue.text: We, full of cheek facing attack, may be anything but serious

indicators.note: full of means the newspaper letters hold the other pieces inside

parts.note: the clue appeared in the Financial Times, which speaks of itself as we: FT
lip is cheeky talk, impudence
to pan is to attack in a review

explanation.surface: We, a cheeky lot, go on the attack and might not be taken seriously.
explanation.walkthrough: 'We' is the newspaper itself, the Financial Times (FT), which holds LIP and PAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Flippant means treating things lightly and with disrespect, so far from grave.

clue.text: One who pampers Mary Cook

parts.note: Molly is a pet form of Mary
to coddle is to cook gently, so one who does is a coddler

explanation.surface: A woman named Mary Cook spoils people.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who indulges another too much is a spoiler of them.

clue.text: Special offer in ad cancelled due to weather

indicators.note: special suggests the letters are made into something different, a rearrangement

explanation.surface: A special offer in an advert was called off because of the weather.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Special offer' reads like shop language; 'Special' is the anagram signal over OFFER IN AD.
explanation.definitionFit: A cricket match or event rained off is abandoned because of rain.

clue.text: Extensive accommodation is dear according to report

indicators.note: according to report signals that the word is said, not written

parts.note: a dear child is a sweet one

explanation.surface: A lavish set of rooms is described as lovely in the report.
explanation.definitionFit: A hotel suite is a set of connected rooms, ample lodging.

clue.text: They need v. still mouths — and v. quiet nostrils possibly!

parts.note: v. is the abbreviation for very, taken as the letter V

indicators.note: possibly hints the letters could form another word when rearranged

explanation.surface: Performers need very still mouths, and perhaps very quiet noses too.
explanation.definitionFit: Performers who throw their voices must keep their lips from moving.

clue.text: The dog who'd provide Pravda with crosswords?

explanation.surface: A question about a dog compiling puzzles for a Soviet newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: Pravda was the Soviet Communist ('Red') paper; a crossword compiler is a setter.
explanation.definitionFit: An Irish breed of gundog with a russet coat; also, fancifully, a communist puzzle compiler.

clue.text: Famous jockey outside home in province

indicators.note: outside puts the jockey's name round the home word

parts.note: Lester Piggott, the celebrated English jockey
in means at home

explanation.surface: A famous jockey stays out of home in an Irish province.
explanation.walkthrough: LEINSTER is one of Ireland's four provinces.
explanation.definitionFit: One of the four historic divisions of Ireland, containing Dublin.

clue.text: Number spinning in funny old picture in part of factory

indicators.note: funny suggests something odd, here a jumble of the letters
spinning turns the number abbreviation round

explanation.surface: Some number turns up in a strange old picture of a factory floor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spinning' makes ON from NO; 'funny' then rearranges ON with IN OLD PICTURE.
explanation.definitionFit: An assembly line is the section of a factory where goods move between workers.

clue.text: Ignores bad patches

indicators.note: bad shows the letters are spoiled and put in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone overlooks rough spots.
explanation.definitionFit: Areas or tracts of land, as in patches of ground.

clue.text: Club ready to settle

parts.note: an iron is a golf club
out can mean available, ready, as a book that is out

explanation.surface: A club is ready to resolve a matter.
explanation.definitionFit: To resolve differences or difficulties is to smooth them away.

clue.text: Understands there will be parking in field?

indicators.note: in puts the parking letter inside the field word

parts.note: grass is a grassy field
P is the sign for parking

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether cars will be parked in a field.
explanation.definitionFit: To grasp an idea is to comprehend it.

clue.text: There's little good in degenerate reprobate

indicators.note: in places the good abbreviation within the debauched man

parts.note: a roue is a dissolute man
G is the abbreviation for good

explanation.surface: There is not much good in a debauched scoundrel.
explanation.definitionFit: A rogue is a dishonest rascal, an unprincipled villain.

clue.text: Severely criticise what office workers do on Fridays?

definitions.text: what office workers do on Fridays?

explanation.surface: Workers get a scolding for their casual Friday clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: To scold harshly is one sense; on casual Fridays staff wear informal clothes instead of suits.

clue.text: Nine housed in filthy dwelling? Many more than nine

indicators.note: housed in puts the numeral inside the dwelling

parts.note: a sty is a pigsty, a filthy home
IX is nine in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Nine live in a squalid home, and there are many more than nine.
explanation.definitionFit: Three score is a number far beyond nine.

clue.text: Take stride outside dance making after-hours conversation?

indicators.note: outside puts the walking word around the dance word

parts.note: to stalk is to walk with long, stiff strides
a hop is an informal dance

explanation.surface: Someone strides away from a dance, chatting late.
explanation.definitionFit: Talk about work, often carried on after work in social settings, is jargon-laden chat.

clue.text: Call on old lover, animated about first hint of reunion

parts.note: an ex is a former partner

indicators.note: about tells us the passionate word goes round the initial letter

parts.note: hot can mean fired up, excited

indicators.note: first hint of takes just the opening letter of reunion

explanation.surface: Someone calls on a former partner, excited at the first sign of reconciliation.
explanation.definitionFit: To call on someone to act is to urge them strongly.

clue.text: Self-absorbed woman gets a scolding locally

indicators.note: absorbed tells us one copy of the name is taken inside the other

parts.note: Sara is a woman's name
self refers back to the woman, so the same name again

explanation.surface: A vain woman is told off in dialect.
explanation.walkthrough: The woman absorbs herself: SARA goes inside SARA, as SA-SARA-RA. 'locally' marks a dialect word.
explanation.definitionFit: In regional English the word is a corruption of certiorari, used for a severe rebuke.

clue.text: Try sex that's kinky? One may scrape bones

indicators.note: kinky means twisted, so the letters are twisted into a new order

explanation.surface: A risqué suggestion about trying something unusual in bed.
explanation.definitionFit: A surgeon's instrument used for scraping bone is the meaning here.
